name: hauksbee-board
description: Hauksbee hardware checks in VS Code: lint, completion and hovers for hauksbee-ci spec TOML, syntax highlighting for .board files, run CI specs and board checks, findings as diagnostics.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Spec completion, hovers and schema linting are pure text analysis and work in an untrusted workspace. Anything that RUNS the hauksbee binaries (the loader lint layer, board-net listing, and the Run CI Spec / Check Board File commands) stays off until the workspace is trusted, because binary discovery falls back to `<workspace>/target/release/hauksbee-ci`: in a trusted workspace the executable can come from the repository tree itself.

hauksbee.path.markdownDescription: Path to the `hauksbee` engine binary. Machine-scoped: a path that gets executed must come from you, not from a checked-in workspace setting. When empty: `HAUKSBEE_BIN`, then PATH, then `target/release/hauksbee` (and `target/debug`) under a workspace folder.

hauksbee.ciPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `hauksbee-ci` spec-runner binary. Machine-scoped: a path that gets executed must come from you, not from a checked-in workspace setting. When empty: `HAUKSBEE_CI_BIN`, then PATH, then `target/release/hauksbee-ci` (and `target/debug`) under a workspace folder.

hauksbee.spec.loaderCheck.markdownDescription:
When to validate a spec with the real `hauksbee-ci` loader (the always-on schema lint needs no binary, and is unaffected). `onSave` runs it on save, but only in a trusted workspace, only when the schema lint is already clean, and never for a spec that declares an output file. `onCommand` restricts it to **Hauksbee: Validate CI Spec**.

Note: `hauksbee-ci run` has no load-only mode, so a spec that loads cleanly goes on into a co-simulation, and one that finishes inside the timeout has genuinely run.

hauksbee.spec.loaderTimeoutMs.markdownDescription: How long to give `hauksbee-ci` to reject a spec before assuming it loaded. `hauksbee-ci run` has no load-only mode, so a clean spec goes straight into a co-simulation; reaching the timeout is read as "the spec loaded" and the child is stopped (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL). Lower it to shorten the window in which a fast co-simulation could run to completion.
